classification.description: Data validation using Python type hints

plan.architecture_summary: Pydantic is Python's standard data validation and serialization library based on type annotations. The repository consists of two main parts: `pydantic-core` (a Rust library providing fast core parsing and validation logic) and `pydantic` (the high-level Python library). The Python codebase handles model construction (BaseModel), field validation decorators (@field_validator, @model_validator), JSON schema generation (GenerateJsonSchema), custom types (networks, types), and schema resolution (_internal/_generate_schema.py). Pytest test suites reside under tests/ to verify validation behavior, typing support, and schema generation.

key_directories.purpose: Main Python package source code containing BaseModel, field definitions, decorators, types, and schema generators
Internal framework utilities for schema generation, model construction, dataclasses, and generics
Rust repository/submodule powering core validation and serialization logic
Pytest test suite covering model validation, types, JSON Schema generation, and decorators

issues.title: `HttpUrl.path` differs from same-named argument in the factory method
issues.why: Pure Python issue in URL type definition, easy to reproduce and fix without touching Rust code.
issues.approach: Inspect HttpUrl and Url.build() path handling in pydantic/networks.py. Ensure consistent handling of leading slashes between .path attribute readouts and path parameter values accepted by HttpUrl.build(). Add unit tests in tests/test_networks.py.

issues.title: Type checkers complain when invoking super().method() if method was decorated with @model_validator
issues.why: Great fit for learning Python type hint decorators and validating behavior against static type checkers.
issues.approach: Check overload type signatures of @model_validator decorator in pydantic/functional_validators.py. Adjust return type annotations to ensure static type checkers (mypy, pyright) correctly recognize method calls via super().

issues.title: model_json_schema() raises PydanticOmit when a shared PEP 695 alias of SkipJsonSchema is used in two fields
issues.why: Python-focused issue in JSON Schema generation handling modern Python PEP 695 type aliases.
issues.approach: Locate SkipJsonSchema and PydanticOmit handling in pydantic/json_schema.py. Ensure that when a shared PEP 695 type alias containing SkipJsonSchema is used across multiple model fields, schema omission is applied cleanly without raising unhandled PydanticOmit errors.

issues.title: Serialization JSON Schema omits null for an unless-none serializer on an Any field
issues.why: Direct logic fix in Pydantic's Python JSON schema generator with straightforward test assertions.
issues.approach: Examine how `unless-none` serialization mode affects nullability in pydantic/json_schema.py. Update schema logic so `null` is included in the JSON Schema for `Any` fields when using `unless-none` serializers, and add pytest cases in tests/test_json_schema.py.

first_timer_insights: Successful first PRs range from single-line documentation fixes (`docs/contributing.md`) to small bug fixes in `pydantic/json_schema.py` or test cleanups in `tests/`.
Maintainers value strict adherence to PR title formatting guidelines since titles automatically populate the changelog.
caveats: PRs addressing existing open issues require assignment from maintainers before submission; unassigned PRs are automatically closed by automated CI workflows.
Rust toolchain is required if building or making changes inside pydantic-core.
Windows users need Git core.symlinks enabled to support symlinked tests between tests/ and pydantic-core/tests.
